definitions.explanation: A person one has known for a long time, or the relationship of having known someone for many years. A somewhat literary or formal word.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}とは{旧知|きゅうち}の{仲|なか}だ。
examples.english: He and I are old acquaintances.

examples.japanese: {旧知|きゅうち}の{友人|ゆうじん}と{久|ひさ}しぶりに{再会|さいかい}した。
examples.english: I reunited with an old friend after a long time.

examples.japanese: {二人|ふたり}は{旧知|きゅうち}の{間柄|あいだがら}で、{学生|がくせい}{時代|じだい}からの{付|つ}き{合|あ}いだという。
examples.english: The two are old acquaintances, having been friends since their student days.

notes:
A formal or literary word for a long-standing acquaintance or friendship. Composed of {旧|きゅう} (old/former) + {知|ち} (knowing/acquaintance). Often appears in set phrases like {旧知|きゅうち}の{仲|なか} or {旧知|きゅうち}の{間柄|あいだがら}.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {旧知|きゅうち}の{仲|なか}: an old acquaintanceship
- {旧知|きゅうち}の{間柄|あいだがら}: a long-standing relationship
- {旧知|きゅうち}の{友人|ゆうじん}: an old friend
- {旧知|きゅうち}を{温|あたた}める: to renew an old friendship

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {知|し}り{合|あ}い: acquaintance — everyday word, no implication of length
- {旧友|きゅうゆう}: old friend — specifically a friend, not just an acquaintance
- {幼馴染|おさななじみ}: childhood friend — friends since childhood specifically
- {顔見知|かおみし}り: someone one knows by face — casual and superficial acquaintance

REGISTER:
Formal and slightly literary. More common in written Japanese, news, and formal speech than in casual conversation.
